input_signals.name: GoodwillWeightedAccrualAggression
input_signals.expression: MUL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accruals are most toxic in firms whose intangible base is acquired (goodwill) rather than organically generated, since purchase accounting supplies discretionary allocations and deferred impairments that amplify accrual-based earnings inflation.
input_signals.reasoning: The goodwill rank acts as an intensity weight on the accrual channel, so pure high-accrual firms with no acquired intangibles get muted scores while acquisitive, accrual-inflated firms are pushed to the short leg. This isolates the accounting-driven component of intangible-related earnings from productive internal investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashGrossProfitOnIntangibleCapital
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(ib, oancf)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Productive intangible investment should show up as cash-realized gross profit per dollar of true (tangible plus capitalized-intangible) capital; stripping accruals out of the profit numerator and adding the R&D stock to the capital base separates firms whose intangible spending actually earns a return from those whose profitability is an accrual artifact.
input_signals.reasoning: The numerator converts gross profit to a cash basis by removing the accrual wedge, and the denominator restates the invested-capital base to include off-balance-sheet intangible capital, so the ratio is an intangible-capital return on cash profits rather than an additive blend of two anomalies. It penalizes high-accrual "profitable" firms and high-R&D firms whose intangible stock generates no cash gross margin, while rewarding cheap, cash-productive innovators.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), sub( ib, oancf ) ), add( at, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: IntangibleOpacityGatedAccrual
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The accrual mispricing is not uniform across firms: it is strongest where intangible spending (R&D plus advertising) makes reported earnings hardest to interpret, so the accrual signal should be amplified for intangible-opaque firms and switched off for transparent, tangible-asset firms.
input_signals.reasoning: The industry z-scored, winsorized accrual quality term carries the sign while the industry rank of intangible intensity acts as a bounded [0,1] amplification gate, producing a true moderation structure rather than an equal-weight difference of two standalone anomalies. Both legs are industry-neutral, so the signal does not proxy for sector membership, and adding advertising broadens the opacity proxy beyond R&D-reporting firms, which supports coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ) ) )

input_signals.name: AcquiredIntangibleAccrualFlow
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The damaging combination is contemporaneous: firms booking large additions to acquired intangibles while simultaneously reporting accrual-heavy earnings are using purchase accounting and allocation discretion to manufacture income that later reverses through impairment.
input_signals.reasoning: Gen 0's goodwill-level weighting produced the best cross-sectional slope but a modest alpha, partly because the large mass of zero-goodwill firms compressed the short leg; switching to the intangible-addition flow and ranking both legs spreads firms across the sort and dates the mechanism to the acquisition year. It changes the economic channel from "stock of acquired intangibles" to "acquisition-year accounting discretion."
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( delta( coalesce( intan, 0 ), 1 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: SustainedRnDRampCleanAccruals
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Commitment to intangible investment is revealed by a sustained multi-year ramp in R&D intensity, not by a single-year level or a reporting dummy; firms steadily raising intangible investment while keeping earnings cash-backed are building real capability, whereas a rising accrual base alongside flat investment signals managed earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the tie-saturated TS_COUNT dummy with a five-year TREND yields a continuous, well-spread commitment measure in which non-R&D firms sit at the middle (zero slope) rather than at an artificial extreme, fixing the degeneracy the critic identified. The five-year slope also avoids the noise that killed the earlier ACCEL construction, so it tests the persistence-versus-level design question with a statistically usable estimator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( trend( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 5 ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: MarginBackedIntangibleAccrual
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross margin is the realized output of intangible capital — brand, patents, process knowledge — rather than its input cost; firms with industry-high margins whose earnings are cash-backed hold proven intangible capital, whereas high margins accompanied by accruals are a recognition-timing artifact.
input_signals.reasoning: Every prior intangible leg has been an input-spending measure (xrd, xad, intan), which conflates spending with productivity and excludes firms that never report R&D; using industry-ranked gross margin flips to an output-based intangible proxy with near-universal coverage. Industry ranking is essential so the leg measures firm-specific pricing power instead of sector cost structure, and pairing it with accrual cleanliness distinguishes durable margins from margins created by revenue recognition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: IndustryIntangibleTechAccrual
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 1)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), IND_ADJ(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The accrual–intangible interaction may be a property of the production technology rather than of the individual filer: in intangible-intensive industries, earnings are hard to interpret for every firm, so accrual quality carries more pricing information there than in tangible industries — including for firms that report no R&D at all.
input_signals.reasoning: Subtracting the industry-demeaned R&D intensity from the raw value recovers the industry-mean intangible intensity, giving an intangible gate that is defined for every firm and therefore repairs the reporting-dummy degeneracy that broke the advertising version, while keeping the firm-level accrual signal as the signed leg. It is also a sharp economic test: if the interaction is industry-level, future refinements should condition on technology rather than on firm-reported spending; if it vanishes, the effect is firm-specific and the search should stay with own-firm intangible capital.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), 1 ) ), rank( sub( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), ind_adj( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: InnovatorAccrualDebtStrain
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), DELTA(dlc, 1)), at), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms cannot collateralize their assets, so when reported income is accrual-supported *and* the firm is simultaneously drawing on short-term debt, the innovation program is being funded by strained external liquidity and is likely to be cut, which the market prices too late.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a financing-strain channel rather than the mirror of an existing investment-trend corner: the signed leg combines accrual earnings with short-term debt draw, and intangible intensity enters only as a bounded amplifier because the collateral problem is specific to firms whose assets are knowledge. The signed continuous leg supplies a linear cross-sectional slope while the gate concentrates the effect where the mechanism applies, so both evidence forms are addressed without recycling the R&D-trend construction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( sub( ib, oancf ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ) )

input_signals.name: MatureInnovationPayoffCleanAccrual
input_signals.expression: MUL(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible capital has a vintage: firms whose accumulated R&D stock is large relative to current-year spending are in the payoff phase, and if their earnings are cash-backed the payoff is real and unrecognized on the balance sheet, whereas ramp-phase spenders have no verified output yet.
input_signals.reasoning: Every intangible leg in the archive measures scale (stock or flow relative to assets, equity, or earnings); this measures the *stage* of the intangible program via the rank gap between accumulated stock and current outlay, which is a distinct economic state and leaves non-R&D firms neutral at zero rather than at an artificial extreme. Pairing maturity with accrual cleanliness tests whether the archive's long-side premium is compensation for unrecognized proven capital rather than for investment intensity per se.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sub( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ConsistentCashBackedInnovator
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 0), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: For a firm whose capital is intangible, the credible quality signal is not the size of this year's accrual but the *frequency* with which earnings have been fully backed by cash: a firm that has produced cash-exceeding-earnings in most of the last five years has demonstrably productive intangible investment rather than favorable one-year working-capital timing.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual leg becomes a discrete count of conservative-reporting years, a state variable measuring reliability rather than magnitude, which is economically different from both the one-year level and a moving average and is immune to a single outlier year driving the rank. This also changes portfolio composition materially — persistent conservatives, not firms with one large negative accrual — so it is a substantive test of whether the archive's long-side alpha reflects durable earnings quality or transitory accrual timing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( ts_sum( indicator( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), 0 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: UnderAmortizedIntangibleAccrual
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(dp, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquired intangibles that sit on the balance sheet without a commensurate amortization charge are unverified carrying value; when such under-amortization coincides with accrual-supported earnings, reported income is doubly overstated and will be corrected through impairment.
input_signals.reasoning: The intangible leg is now an expense-treatment mismatch — capitalized intangible intensity in excess of the firm's total D&A burden — which is neither a growth variable (the gen-3 attribution failure) nor a deflator variant of goodwill intensity, and it is well defined and stable for low- or negative-equity firms because both components are asset-scaled ranks. It targets the accounting mechanism the theme names explicitly, the expense-treatment channel, and pairs it with the accrual channel so neither leg alone can produce the signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), sub( rank( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( dp, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: BalanceSheetAccrualInnovator
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: If the interaction reflects real accounting economics rather than an artifact of cash-flow-statement mechanics, it must hold when accruals are measured from successive balance sheets, which also extends the mechanism to the pre-cash-flow-statement era and to firms with incomplete oancf reporting.
input_signals.reasoning: Every accrual leg in the archive is built from oancf, which restricts the usable sample (coverage ~0.09) and embeds Compustat's reporting-format changes; the one signal that avoided oancf had materially higher coverage (0.113), so this is a measurement-basis and sample-length test with real power implications for ls_talpha. It is not a cosmetic change: the balance-sheet definition captures working-capital accruals including non-cash items that never pass through oancf, and disagreement between the two versions would localize the mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ), dp ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: BalanceSheetConservatismPersistence
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at)), 0), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable earnings quality for an intangible-intensive firm is revealed by how many of the last five years its balance sheet failed to accumulate accruals; measured on the balance sheet rather than the cash-flow statement, this reliability state should predict returns over a longer sample and across firms that never reported oancf.
input_signals.reasoning: The conservatism-count leg produced the archive's best cross-sectional slope (3.76) but only 3.5% alpha, and the diagnosis was that its oancf-based construction restricted the sample precisely where power is gained; rebuilding the count on the Sloan accrual tests whether persistence and magnitude were competing because of measurement, not economics. It is a different variable from the gen-5 winner (a five-year frequency state, not a one-year magnitude), so the portfolios and the failure mode differ.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( ts_sum( indicator( neg( ratio( sub( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ), dp ), at ) ), 0 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CumulativeAccrualBloatInnovator
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 3), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual distortion accumulates: a firm that has added working-capital accruals for three consecutive years has a balance sheet carrying an unwound stock of soft assets, and for intangible-intensive firms — whose real assets are invisible — this accumulated bloat is the cleanest evidence that reported earnings were accounting-driven.
input_signals.reasoning: Cumulating the same Sloan accrual over three years converts a flow into an accrual stock (the economic content of the net-operating-assets anomaly) while keeping the intangible-capital partner and the sample advantage of the balance-sheet definition. This is a distinct economic quantity from the one-year accrual, and it directly tests whether the gen-5 result is about this year's timing or about a multi-year unwinding overhang.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ts_sum( ratio( sub( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ), dp ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: BrandPlusResearchCapitalCleanAccrual
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: If the long-side premium is compensation for unrecognized intangible capital generally, then adding accumulated advertising to accumulated R&D should broaden the long leg into consumer and media firms without diluting it; if the premium is specific to research, the broader stock will weaken it.
input_signals.reasoning: Brand capital is expensed under the same accounting convention as R&D, so the hidden-capital hypothesis predicts both stocks belong in the intangible leg, and combining them as a five-year cumulative flow avoids the reporting-dummy degeneracy that killed the earlier advertising-only attempt. Pairing it with the balance-sheet accrual keeps the sample and measurement advantages of the gen-5 winner, so the comparison isolates the intangible definition alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ), dp ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OperatingCycleBloatInnovator
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A knowledge-intensive firm should convert sales to cash quickly; when such a firm carries many months of non-cash working capital per dollar of revenue, its reported revenue is sitting in receivables and inventory rather than in the bank, and its earnings are recognition-driven.
input_signals.reasoning: Removing cash from the numerator and deflating by sales converts the leg from the published net-operating-assets ratio (whose cross-sectional variation is dominated by cash holdings) into an operating-cycle length measure, so the signal can no longer be a disguised cash-richness sort. It remains a level state variable computable without cash-flow-statement data, preserving the coverage advantage that drove the gen-5 improvement, and the intangible gate restricts the claim to firms for which a long operating cycle is economically anomalous.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), sale ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: MarginBackedBalanceSheetAccrual
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross margin is the realized output of intangible capital and is observable for every firm, including non-reporters of R&D; combined with balance-sheet-verified clean accruals it should identify proven, cash-consistent pricing power rather than recognition-timing.
input_signals.reasoning: The industry-ranked margin leg holds the archive record for cross-sectional slope (4.29) but delivered only 2.7% alpha when paired with the oancf wedge, and the gen-5 evidence attributes exactly that kind of alpha shortfall to accrual measurement and sample length. If the upgrade transfers, this is the batch's best candidate for simultaneously strong fmb_tstat and ls_talpha, and its output-based intangible proxy makes the result independent of R&D disclosure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ), dp ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExcessWorkingCapitalGrowthInnovator
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Working capital that grows faster than sales is accrual build-up that the business does not justify, and in intangible-intensive firms — which need little working capital at all — such excess growth marks earnings created by recognition rather than by demand.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the flaw in the gen-4 abnormal-accrual attempt: both terms are now growth rates in identical units, so the construction is a genuine expectation-model residual rather than a difference of incomparable ranks, and no raw growth variable enters with an unintended positive loading. It uses only balance-sheet and income-statement inputs, retaining the coverage advantage (≈0.12) that has accompanied every recent improvement.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( sub( growth( sub( act, che ), 1 ), growth( sale, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: KnowledgeShareOfCapitalProgramCleanAccrual
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), dp))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: What determines how badly accounting misrepresents a firm is the knowledge share of its capital program — expensed research relative to research plus the depreciation charge on physical capital — because a firm consuming physical capital gets a recognized asset base while a firm consuming research gets none; among such knowledge-weighted firms, clean accruals confirm the reported earnings are conservative rather than managed.
input_signals.reasoning:
This intangible leg is new to the archive in both variable set and economics: it is a bounded composition measure of the firm's investment mix (knowledge versus physical capital consumption) rather than any spending-to-assets or spending-to-equity intensity, so it is not a monotone transform of an existing leg and it reorders capital-light service firms against R&D-heavy manufacturers. It is defined for every firm, keeps the balance-sheet-accrual coverage advantage, and pairs the expense-treatment channel (what gets capitalized) directly with the accrual channel.
REASONING_END: none
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), dp ) ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ), dp ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: InvisibleVersusAccrualExpansion
input_signals.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 1), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms expand in two accounting-visible ways: by adding expensed intangible investment, which shows up nowhere on the balance sheet, or by accumulating working-capital accruals, which inflate both assets and reported income; the firm whose expansion is invisible rather than accrual-based is systematically undervalued.
input_signals.reasoning:
This is a single centered composition variable contrasting two channels of growth rather than a gate multiplied by a signed leg, so it is structurally unlike every conditional interaction in the archive and cannot be produced by swapping the accrual definition into an existing signal. Both components are same-year flows scaled by assets and then ranked, so the contrast is unit-consistent, spans the full cross-section, and places accrual-financed expanders at the short pole and quiet invisible investors at the long pole.
REASONING_END: none
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( rank( ratio( delta( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 1 ), at ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ), dp ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: KnowledgeStockShareCleanAccrual
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), SUB(SUB(at, act), COALESCE(intan, 0))))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The stock analogue of the knowledge share — accumulated research capital relative to that capital plus the firm's recognized long-lived tangible base — measures what fraction of a firm's productive assets is missing from the balance sheet, and this fraction should govern how badly earnings-anchored investors misprice a cash-consistent firm.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-7 knowledge share is a flow ratio built on this year's depreciation charge, so it is sensitive to asset age; expressing the same economics as a stock composition (research capital versus non-current tangible assets, with purchased intangibles removed so only unrecognized capital counts) tests whether the flow result was an amortization-timing artifact. It remains bounded, defined for all firms, and free of cash-flow-statement inputs, so it preserves the coverage that has accompanied every recent gain.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), add( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), sub( sub( at, act ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ) ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ), dp ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: StableMarginMoatCleanAccrual
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable intangible capital reveals itself as *stable* pricing power, not merely high pricing power: a firm whose gross margin barely varies over five years holds a genuine moat, and when its earnings are also cash-consistent the market underprices the durability.
input_signals.reasoning: The margin-level leg produced the best slope in the archive but an unusually poor Sharpe ratio (0.08), which points to volatile, industry-tilted portfolio composition rather than to a weak mechanism; margin stability is a second-moment output measure of intangible capital that no signal has tested and that should select steadier firms, improving spread reliability while retaining the disclosure-independent coverage of the margin family. It is a different economic claim from margin level — durability of advantage rather than size of advantage.

input_signals.hypothesis: Measured over three years, a firm either expanded its unrecognized investment programme or expanded its accrual base; the contrast between these two expansion channels over a horizon long enough to smooth reporting noise should predict returns more reliably than the one-year contrast.
input_signals.reasoning:
This is the horizon test the previous version claimed but did not implement: both legs are now three-year *expansions* — the three-year change in R&D spending and the three-year cumulative accrual — so the comparison against the gen-7 one-year signal isolates horizon alone and cannot collapse into the archived stock-level-times-cumulative-accrual product. It retains the centered difference form, whose full-cross-section coverage and 5.0% alpha at t=5.24 make it one of the study's most promising structures.

input_signals.expression: MIN(MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), dp))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Productive, unrecognized intangible capital requires all three conditions at once — a knowledge-weighted capital programme, earnings not supported by accruals, and margins that prove the capital earns a return — so a firm should be credited only to the extent of its weakest condition, with no compensation across dimensions.
input_signals.reasoning:
The previous triple product was compensatory and therefore did not test the stated claim; nesting MIN implements the conjunctive (Leontief) form exactly, so a high margin rank can no longer offset accrual-supported earnings. This is the only structure in the study that can distinguish "all three needed" from "weighted average of three," and because the three legs individually own the best slope and the best alphas in the archive, the answer determines how the final generation should combine them.

input_signals.hypothesis: Much intangible investment never appears as reported R&D — it is buried in overhead — so the gap between gross profit and net income measures total expensed investment and overhead conservatism; firms where this gap is large relative to assets and whose accruals are clean have the most understated earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: Every intangible leg in the archive depends on disclosed xrd, xad, or intan, which excludes the large population of firms that invest in organizational and human capital through selling and administrative spend; this leg is disclosure-independent, has near-universal coverage, and captures the same expense-treatment distortion the theme names. It is a genuinely new intangible proxy rather than a re-deflation of R&D, and pairing it with the accrual leg keeps the productive-versus-accounting separation intact.

input_signals.hypothesis: Organizational, human and brand capital are built through overhead spending that is expensed with no disclosure line of its own; removing reported R&D from the gross-profit-minus-net-income gap isolates precisely this undisclosed investment, and where it is large and accruals are clean, earnings understate economic capital.
input_signals.reasoning:
Every intangible leg in the archive is either disclosed R&D, disclosed advertising, or purchased intangibles, so the study cannot currently say whether the conservatism premium exists for the majority of firms that invest without an R&D line; subtracting xrd makes the leg orthogonal to the entire R&D family rather than a redeflation of it. It has near-universal coverage and, paired with the balance-sheet accrual, keeps the productive-versus-accounting separation while testing the mechanism in a population the study has never reached.

input_signals.hypothesis: A firm currently expensing more investment than its own five-year norm has depressed earnings for investment reasons rather than for operating reasons, and when the accrual base is simultaneously clean the depressed earnings are unambiguously conservative rather than managed.
input_signals.reasoning:
All intangible legs tested so far are cross-sectional levels, which conflate business model with investment behaviour; the deviation of expensed investment intensity from the firm's own norm identifies firms whose *current* reported earnings are temporarily understated, which is the state in which earnings-anchored mispricing should be largest. Both legs are firm-relative or peer-relative in different ways, so the interaction is not a re-weighting of the archive's level-times-level structure.

input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), ib), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Understated earnings are only informative when they are also credible, so a firm should be credited by the weaker of two conditions — how much investment it expenses and how free of accruals its balance sheet is — with no compensation between them.
input_signals.reasoning:
The gen-8 weakest-link test produced the study's best cross-sectional slope (4.33) but weak alpha, and the diagnosis is specific: the alpha loss came from the third, margin-level channel, which has destroyed alpha in every specification it has entered, not from the conjunctive form itself. Applying the same form to two channels only — one of which is the new expensed-investment leg — is the decisive test of that diagnosis and, if correct, should deliver a high slope together with the family's usual 5–6% alpha.
